failures.criterion: The architect's question: why smoke-replay.sh remote mode's read-back misses a /v1/messages/send publish; fail if it is a defect. The script's remote mode is part of what this PR delivers.
failures.evidence: No message is lost; the script is broken. replay_read reads its cursor from ${2:-} (packages/pi-envoy/scripts/smoke-replay.sh:712), but publish calls replay_read "$watermark" (line 774), which passes the cursor as $1. The /v1/replay request therefore carries no 'after', and the route only starts a cursor and returns no messages. Reproduce with the committed script: run it in remote mode against a loopback listener and natsd built from this head (SMOKE_REPLAY_ENVOY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port> SMOKE_REPLAY_NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:<port> bash packages/pi-envoy/scripts/smoke-replay.sh) -> exit 1, 'SMOKE REPLAY FAIL (leg-1-reconnect): /v1/replay after 0 does not hold 9bfb96ed…', while the answer shows last_seq 1 and messages []. The same read-back driven 67 times missed 67 of 67, and each stayed missing for 10 s while the stream held every message (raw STREAM.MSG.GET next_by_subj returns each). The same 150 sends with 'after' actually sent were all found by the first read-back. Fix: ${2:-} -> ${1:-} in replay_read. The next round re-runs remote mode as committed. No red test in a suite: a test of the script's text is not allowed, and the committed script's own remote run is the failing check.
